section_summary: This section focuses on post-World War II territorial sovereignty, boundaries, and administrative disposition of islands surrounding Japan proper. It includes diplomatic correspondence, petitions regarding the Northern Territories (Kurile Islands) and the Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa), congressional inquiries regarding national area and population statistics, and extensive historical and geographical studies prepared by the Japanese Foreign Office on the Nansei, Bonin, and Volcano Island groups.

subfiles.about: Acknowledgement of State Department letters regarding military government and outlying Pacific islands.
subfiles.summary: Navy Department confirms incorporation of State Department suggestions into the political directive for outlying islands.
subfiles.title: Letter from Chief of Naval Operations to James Clement Dunn

subfiles.about: Consular dispatch raising questions of international law regarding missionary influence and political sovereignty claims in the Pacific.
subfiles.summary: Consul Sokobin critiques George H. Blakeslee's article arguing that American missionary activity in the Pacific justified political sovereignty.
subfiles.title: Questions of International Law and of American Policy Raised by Dr. George H. Blakeslee's Article

subfiles.about: Congressional inquiry requesting data on Japan's total area and population.
subfiles.summary: Representative LaFollette forwards a constituent inquiry requesting official figures on the area and population of Japan and its holdings.
subfiles.title: Inquiry regarding the Area and Population of Japan

subfiles.about: Department of State transmittal providing statistical tables of Japan's empire area and population.
subfiles.from: Special Assistant to Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: State Department replies to Representative LaFollette with detailed statistical tables detailing the areas and 1937 populations of Japan Proper and its overseas possessions.
subfiles.title: Reply to Representative LaFollette on Area and Population of Japanese Empire

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum transferring a packet of Japanese scenic postcards.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum forwarding 20 postcards of the Japanese coast near Atami for possible military intelligence use by G-2 or ONI.
subfiles.title: Transmission of Postcards of Japanese Coast near Atami

subfiles.about: Transmittal of coast view postcards from the State Department to Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Division of Foreign Activity Correlation transmits coastal postcards near Atami to the Director of Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.title: Postcards of the Japanese Coast near Atami

subfiles.about: New York Times inquiry concerning Soviet troop patrols around Hokkaido and adjacent islands.
subfiles.summary: Journalist queries Under Secretary Acheson on reported Soviet patrol agreements and occupation of islands off Hokkaido and Sakhalin.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Soviet Troops Patrolling Islands near Hokkaido

subfiles.about: Brief departmental acknowledgement of a press inquiry on Hokkaido boundary issues.
subfiles.summary: Department of State acknowledges Dinsmore's letter regarding the boundary between Hokkaido and Soviet-occupied territory.
subfiles.title: Acknowledgement to Herman H. Dinsmore

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting an Okinawan petition requesting restoration to Japan.
subfiles.summary: US Political Adviser transmits a petition from Baron Chosuke Iye and Ryoko Nakayoshi urging the return of Okinawa to Japanese administration.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 660: Transmitting Petition of Certain Okinawans

subfiles.about: Petition to Supreme Commander MacArthur requesting the return of Okinawa to Japanese administration.
subfiles.from: Baron Chosuke Iye, Ryoko Nakayoshi, and Okinawan residents
subfiles.summary: Okinawan residents in Japan express gratitude for American relief while requesting that Okinawa be returned to Japanese civil governance, detailing cultural, historical, and racial ties, accompanied by signed petition sheets.
subfiles.title: Petition to General MacArthur for the Return of Okinawa to Japan

subfiles.about: Administrative distribution record form for Tokyo Despatch No. 891.
subfiles.summary: Division routing slip and distribution cover sheet for documents relating to Tokyo Despatch No. 891.
subfiles.title: Department of State Distribution Record Sheet

subfiles.about: Central records notice designating a replacement copy of an action despatch.
subfiles.summary: Notice stating that the attached document serves as the official record copy replacing an unreturned action copy.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting a petition regarding the restoration of northern islands adjacent to Hokkaido.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Political Adviser transmits a petition for the return of northern islands, assessing it as officially inspired by the Japanese Foreign Office.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 891: Transmitting Petition for Restoration of Islands Belonging to Hokkaido

subfiles.about: Petition to General MacArthur appealing for the return of Soviet-occupied islands adjacent to Nemuro and Hokkaido.
subfiles.from: The Committee of Petition for the Restoration of Islands Belonging to Hokkaido
subfiles.summary: Citizens and refugees from Nemuro petition MacArthur to restore Etorofu, Kunashiri, and the Habomai group from Soviet occupation, highlighting severe fishery distress and family displacement.
subfiles.title: Petition to General MacArthur for the Restoration of Islands Belonging to Hokkaido

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch forwarding a petition from Hokkaido members of the Japanese Diet.
subfiles.summary: US Political Adviser forwards an English petition submitted by Takeshi Hoshina on behalf of Hokkaido Diet representatives requesting the return of adjacent islands.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 957: Forwarding Copy of Petition for Restoration of Islands Belonging to Hokkaido

subfiles.about: Diet members' petition to General MacArthur arguing for Japanese sovereignty over the Shikotan group and Southern Kuriles.
subfiles.from: Takeshi Hoshina and Members of the House of Representatives from Hokkaido
subfiles.summary: Elected Hokkaido representatives set forth historical treaties and economic dependency on northern fishing grounds, asking MacArthur to intercede against permanent Soviet annexation.
subfiles.title: Petition by Hokkaido Diet Members for Return of Shikotan and Southern Kuriles

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch forwarding Parts II and III of a Japanese Foreign Office monograph on minor adjacent islands.
subfiles.summary: US Political Adviser transmits Parts II and III of the Japanese Foreign Office study on minor islands adjacent to Japan proper.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 1166: Minor Islands Adjacent to Japan

subfiles.about: Official study of the geography, history, and status of the Ryukyu and Nansei Islands.
subfiles.summary: Comprehensive Japanese Foreign Office study demonstrating the physical geography, anthropology, history, and prewar integration of the Nansei and Ryukyu Islands with Japan. It documents historical relations with China and Japan, Meiji-era diplomatic settlements, and modern economic and educational ties to support Japanese retention.
subfiles.title: Minor Islands Adjacent to Japan Proper, Part II: Ryukyu and Other Nansei Islands

subfiles.about: Official study of the geography, history, and sovereign status of the Bonin and Volcano island groups.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Foreign Office survey detailing early Japanese discovery and settlement of the Bonin and Volcano groups, 19th-century diplomatic negotiations with Britain and the United States, and administrative integration under Tokyo Prefecture.
subfiles.title: Minor Islands Adjacent to Japan Proper, Part III: The Bonin Island Group, The Volcano Island Group
